This is an all-day recipe I like to do on the weekends or for special occasions to make delicious pulled pork for carnitas. It uses the blade steak, which features meat, cut-open shoulder bone and plenty of marbled fat. I look for the cuts with the ideal amounts of each, usually about 15% bone, 60% meat, 25% fat. Because it requires some additional butchering still to seperate components it is often a good value at the market. If you don't see blade steaks or want skip a step, just buy some bone broth and pork shoulder instead.

Stock-Pot Carnitas

2 - 3 lbs pork blade steak
1 Jumbo size yellow onion
2 - 4 roasted whole green chiles
2 chipotles in adobo sauce
5 - 10 cloves garlic
12oz of pale or bitter ale
12oz orange juice
1 tablespoon of salsa roja
1 tsp salt
1 tsp black pepper
1 tsp cumin
1 tsp coriander
1 tsp oregano
1/2 tsp chili powder
2 Bay leaves 1 splash red wine

Cut the bones out of the steaks, cleaning as much of the meat and fat off as you can. If the bone is shattered, look for embedded shards in the meat. Leaving a bit on the bone is fine. Cover the bones with water and a pinch of salt in a pot and bring to a boil, then add water to about 12-16ozs and keep warm and covered for an hour. During this time, prepare the meat and fat.

Trim the fat from the meat, and place in a small pot on low heat until it runs clear, stirring often. When the fat has melted, let cool and strain into a large, warmed stock pot. While waiting for the fat to render, cut the meat into even pieces, dice the onion and the garlic cloves.

Strain the rendered fat into a stock pot on high heat and add the pork. Stir occasionally until browning occurs, then add the bone broth. Add the chipotles and adobo sauce. Add the ale and the onions. Stir and bring to temp, then add the orange juice, salsa, wine, salt and spices. Note: wines labeled "cooking wines" will have the salt included.

Simmer for 6 - 8 hours, stirring and mashing occasionally until all ingredients are finely shredded and about 85-90% of the liquid is gone. Leave the lid off initially, supplement with a splash more of beer and or orange juice, then cover until it's close to finished. Serve with tortillas, salsa, shredded cheese, radish slices, a piece of lime and an ice cold beer.
